evidence.intree_statement: Record Reflective {C : Category} (S : Subcategory C) := { reflective_full : Construction.Subcategory.Full C S; reflector : C ⟶ Sub C S; reflective_adj : reflector ⊣ Incl C S }.

statement_record.book: A subcategory A of B is reflective when the inclusion K : A -> B has a left adjoint F (the reflector); the adjunction <F, K, phi> is a reflection of B in A. Equivalent descriptions: a functor R : B -> B with values in A and a natural bijection A(Rb, a) ≅ B(b, a); or, for each b, a universal arrow eta_b : b -> Rb to the subcategory.
statement_record.intree: Record Reflective bundles fullness of the subcategory, the reflector C ⟶ Sub C S, and the adjunction reflector ⊣ Incl C S (Construction/Reflective.v:60-64), over Construction/Subcategory.v's Sub/Incl.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger (narrower): the record additionally demands fullness of the subcategory, whereas Mac Lane defines reflectivity for an arbitrary subcategory and treats fullness as a separate condition (his remark2 covers the full case); this matches the modern nLab convention. Mac Lane's two equivalent reformulations (the R : B -> B natural-bijection form and the universal-arrow form) are not separately proven, though the universal-arrow form is recoverable from the general adjunction ⟺ universal-arrows machinery of Theory/Universal/Arrow.v

verifier.notes: Evidence verified verbatim: Construction/Reflective.v:60-64 is `Record Reflective {C : Category} (S : Subcategory C) = { reflective_full : Construction.Subcategory.Full C S; reflector : C ⟶ Sub C S; reflective_adj : reflector ⊣ Incl C S }`, over Construction/Subcategory.v's `Sub`/`Incl` (Incl at :59, `Definition Full` at :69, plus `Full_Implies_Full_Functor`). Both files registered (_CoqProject:59, :71) and compiled (.vo present). The record is genuinely consumed, not decorative: Construction/Localization.v:185,231, Construction/Localization/Universal.v:76, Construction/Reflective/Idempotent.v:166 all take `R : Reflective S`, and Idempotent.v:345 CONSTRUCTS one. HYPOTHESIS DIVERGENCE, disclosed by the classifier and worth restating sharply: Mac Lane defines reflectivity for an ARBITRARY subcategory (his very next sentence — 'since K is always faithful, the counit of a reflection is always epi' — only makes sense in that generality), whereas the in-tree record bundles fullness, so the in-tree notion is strictly narrower.
